page: UpCloud PREMIUM-32xCPU-64GB is a KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Premium family. It features 32 shared AMD EPYC 9575F vCPUs operating at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, with 32 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 400 GB local SSD, and the network configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including AVX512_VNNI and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core and bzip3 single-threaded decompression scoring in the top 10%. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory read bandwidth is also strong, reaching 5608.39 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 230.25 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. However, a key tradeoff is the PassMark memory score, which falls into the bottom 25%, and memory write bandwidth for large uncached blocks, which is average.

This server configuration is suited for compute-intensive workloads that benefit from high parallelization and vector instructions but do not require massive memory footprints, such as batch processing, static web serving, and lightweight LLM inference. In terms of qualitative cost efficiency, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides high compute density, though the shared CPU allocation model may introduce performance variability compared to dedicated resources.
description: UpCloud PREMIUM-32xCPU-64GB is an x86_64 virtual server featuring 32 shared AMD EPYC 9575F vCPUs at 2.0 GHz, 64.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 400 GB local SSD. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, this instance delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance and strong multi-core capabilities, placing in the top 10% and top 25% of benchmarks respectively. While memory read bandwidth is strong, memory write performance and PassMark memory scores represent a relative tradeoff, landing in the bottom 25%. The 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio makes this server suitable for compute-heavy tasks, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression workloads that do not require dedicated CPU allocations.
